verdict.rationale: Stripe documents per-credential controls rather than per-agent ones. Shared payment tokens carry usage limits (currency, maximum amount, expiration window) and can be revoked at any time so a seller can't charge them. Link CLI spends are gated by customer approval of each one-time-use credential. However, these limits are set per token by the issuing agent, not as an aggregate cap the user sets on a given agent, and revocation targets a single token rather than an agent's whole payment authority. Restricted API key permissions scope what an agent can do in an account but are not spend caps. Missing for 10: user-configurable per-agent aggregate spend caps, recurring usage/rate limits per agent, a single control to revoke all of an agent's payment authority, independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can set per-agent spend caps and usage limits and revoke an agent's payment authority instantly

citations.quote: Set usage limits, including currency, maximum amount, and expiration window
Revoke the SPT at any time to prevent the seller from using it to create a payment
Sellers can’t create a payment with a revoked SPT.
Creates a spend request for a specific purchase. The customer approves it, and Link returns a one-time-use payment credential your agent uses to pay.
